Subject: Redwood integration — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Alice — great to speak today, thanks for the time. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Recap (high level)
- Primary use case: customer support augmentation + knowledge retrieval + short-form generation for agent assist.
- P0 requirements: sub-200ms median generation latency for single-turn agent assists, secure keying and audit logs, private data never leaves Acme VPC for regulated flows.
- Evaluation: want to run a 2-week POC with 50k query throughput (burst) to validate cost and quality.

Architecture / integration topics we agreed to follow up on
1) SDK setup & auth
   - We support server-side SDKs (Python/Node/Go) and a lightweight client for browser use-cases.
   - Auth options: short-lived API credentials (recommended for hosted), optional mTLS + private endpoints for Redwood Private.
2) Routing & failover
   - Policy-based routing: latency-first for agent workflows, cost-fallback to smaller quantized model for background batch jobs.
   - Region pinning and automatic fallback to a secondary region on capacity events.
3) Structured output & tool-calling
   - We support JSON-schema-based structured responses and function/tool-calling primitives (streamed).
   - We'll share an example schema for your agent actions and the code samples for validating responses.
4) Embeddings & reranker
   - Recommendation: 1536-dim dense embeddings (or 768 for lower cost) + faiss/ann index.
   - Reranker: hybrid approach — lightweight similarity for recall then a reranking model for precision.
5) Prompt templates & governance
   - Version prompts in a repo (semantic tags), enforce system prompt templates per environment, and apply prompt-injection mitigations in the SDK.
   - Red-team plan: periodic adversarial testing + regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets.

Attachments: redwood-integration-diagram.png (high-level flow), acme-ma-template.pdf (mutual action / SOW template).

Proposed immediate next steps
- Tech deep-dive (45–60m) with your cloud/platform engineering team — propose Tue/Wed next week (see availability below).
- Devs: one-week access to a trial key + a sandbox dataset to verify embeddings/reranker.*
- I'll send a draft MA/POC scope (attached) and a DocuSign link for review.

Availability: Tue 11/23 10–12 PT, Wed 11/24 09–11 PT, Thu 11/25 13–15 PT — which works for your team?

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Subject: RE: Redwood integration — short answers to Acme's follow-ups

Hi team / Alice — answers inline for the items Alice raised. 

1) SDK & auth
   - Server-side recommendation: issue short-lived service JWTs backed by your IdP (OAuth2 client-credentials -> exchange for Redwood short-lived token). This gives auditability and lets you rotate creds centrally. For high-security flows we support mutual TLS + customer-managed private endpoints on Redwood Private.
   - We emit request-level audit logs: request id, user id (when supplied), model, route, token usage. Logs can be forwarded to your SIEM or S3 for retention.

2) Embeddings (100M vectors)
   - Ops patterns: split hot/warm/cold. Keep most-recent or frequently-accessed vectors in an ANN index (faiss/HNSW) on SSD-backed nodes; archive cold vectors to object storage and rebuild smaller indexes on demand or use a hybrid approach with quantized indexes.
   - Managed options: Pinecone/Weaviate/Managed Faiss on k8s; we integrate with common providers and can provide connectors.

3) Reranker metrics
   - Example: similarity-only baseline (recall-focused) gets ~0.78 recall@10 on our KB dataset, adding a single-pass reranker model typically improves nDCG@10 by 12–25% depending on prompt design and reranker size. We'll share a short benchmark artifact.

4) Prompt governance
   - Storage: we recommend storing prompt templates and system prompts in a versioned repo (git) and then use our Prompt API/CLI to push a release (semantic version tag) to environments (dev/stage/prod).
   - Rollout: Canary rollout support (percentage traffic), instant rollback to previous prompt version, and immutable prompt snapshots for audit. SDKs validate schema and can enforce allowed variables/whitelist patterns to reduce injection risk.

5) Red teaming / injection testing
   - Cadence: start with a focused red-team run during POC (2–3 weeks), then quarterly automated fuzzing + manual adversarial sessions.
   - Tooling: internal harness that fuzzes instruction vectors, malicious tokens, and prompt injection patterns; we also provide a prompt-safety layer in the SDK to canonicalize input and policy-check outputs.

Implementation notes / sample patterns
- Structured output: we recommend JSON Schema for the tool-calling responses. Example: {"action":"OPEN_TICKET","fields":{"summary":"string","priority":"enum[low,med,high]"}} — SDK will validate and strip unexpected fields.
- Prompt versioning: tag prompts as v1.2.0-prompts/docs and use the Prompt CLI to promote to stage/prod. Keep a small immutable audit log per request that records prompt_version and prompt_hash.

I'll prep a short artifact with the example schema, an SDK snippet for auth exchange, and a short benchmark for reranker tradeoffs ahead of the deep-dive.
